title: NEVER Buy Boneless Chicken Breasts Again — This Old Butcher Trick Gets You Twice the Meat
description:
🐔 Never buy boneless chicken breasts again. For about the same money, one whole chicken gives you two breasts, two thighs, two drumsticks, two wings and two quarts of broth. All 12 steps are written out below 👇

June had a two-pound pack of boneless breasts in her cart: nine dollars and eighteen cents, four suppers if she was careful. Right next to the scale was a whole chicken, almost five pounds, for twelve cents less. After forty-one years behind a small-town Iowa meat counter, Helen cuts it up with one knife and shows you how to get about ten meals out of it.

⭐ THE 12 STEPS
1. Read the price per pound on the sticker, not the total
2. Pick the right bird: 4 to 5 pounds, plump, cold, tight wrap
3. Do not wash it: pat it dry with paper towels
4. Find the pop: bend the leg back, the hip joint shows you where to cut
5. Split the leg on the fat line: thigh and drumstick
6. The wings: stretch them out and find the shoulder joint
7. The breasts: knife along the breastbone, short gentle strokes
8. One breast, two suppers: split it into thin cutlets
9. Make the broth: back, frame, wing tips, 2 to 3 hours barely simmering
10. Pick the frame: the cooked meat is supper too
11. Freeze it in suppers: one supper per bag, about 9 months
12. The first one is ugly, and that is fine

🍲 WHAT ONE WHOLE CHICKEN GIVES YOU
2 breasts → 4 thin cutlets (4 suppers)
2 thighs + 2 drumsticks → 2 more suppers
2 wings → 1 supper
Back, frame and wing tips → about 2 quarts of real broth and a pot of soup
About 10 meals instead of 4, for the same money

⚠️ Food safety: do not rinse raw chicken (it splashes germs around the sink). Cook chicken to 165°F (thighs are best around 175°F). Get broth into the refrigerator within 2 hours. Thaw frozen chicken in the refrigerator. (USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service guidance.)
